gs-58-en: Are there many ties between the message of salvation and human culture, such that God has spoken according to the culture proper to each epoch and the Church has used the discoveries of different cultures in preaching Christ?
gs-59-en: Is culture to be subordinated to the integral perfection of the human person and to the good of the community and of the whole society?
gs-60-en: Is it especially the duty of Christians in our times to work for economic and political decisions that recognize and satisfy the right of all to a human and social culture in conformity with the dignity of the human person?
gs-61-en: Despite the growing mass and diversity of cultural factors, does each person still have a duty to retain an understanding of the whole human person in which the values of intellect, will, conscience and fraternity are preeminent?
gs-62-en: Can difficulties in harmonizing culture with Christian teaching stimulate the mind to a deeper and more accurate understanding of the faith, and do recent findings of science, history, and philosophy raise new questions affecting life?
gs-63-en: In the economic and social realms, are the dignity and complete vocation of the human person and the welfare of society as a whole to be respected and promoted, since man is the source, center, and purpose of all economic and social life?
gs-64-en: Is attention rightly given today to increasing the production of agricultural and industrial goods and services in order to provide for population growth and to satisfy the increasing desires of the human race?
gs-65-en: Must economic development remain under man's determination and not be left to a few possessing too much economic power, or to the political community alone, or to certain more powerful nations?
gs-66-en: Must strenuous efforts be made, without disregarding the rights of persons or the natural qualities of each country, to remove as quickly as possible the immense economic inequalities that now exist and in many cases are growing?
gs-67-en: Is human labor expended in the production and exchange of goods or in economic services superior to the other elements of economic life, which have only the nature of tools?
gs-68-en: In economic enterprises, should the active sharing of all—owners, employers, management, and labor—in the administration and profits be promoted, without harming the necessary unity of management?
gs-69-en: Did God intend the earth with everything in it for the use of all human beings and peoples, so that under justice and charity created goods should be in abundance for all, with attention always paid to this universal destination of earthly goods?
gs-70-en: Must investments be directed toward procuring employment and sufficient income for the people both now and in the future, and are those who decide on investments bound to keep these objectives in mind?
gs-71-en: Since property and other forms of private ownership of external goods contribute to the expression of the personality, is it very important that access of individuals and communities to some ownership of external goods be fostered?
gs-72-en: Should Christians who take an active part in socio-economic development and fight for justice and charity be convinced that they can make a great contribution to the prosperity of mankind and to the peace of the world?
gs-73-en: Do profound changes in the structure and institutions of peoples, resulting from cultural, economic, and social evolution, greatly influence the life of the political community regarding civil freedom and the common good?
gs-74-en: Do men, families, and the various groups of the civil community need a wider political community for the sake of the common good, since they cannot achieve a truly human life by their own unaided efforts?
gs-75-en: Is it in full conformity with human nature that juridico-political structures provide all citizens, without discrimination, the practical possibility of freely and actively taking part in public affairs and in electing political leaders?
gs-76-en: Especially where a pluralistic society prevails, should there be a correct notion of the relationship between the political community and the Church, and a clear distinction between Christians' tasks as citizens and activities carried out in the name of the Church?
gs-77-en: Facing an hour of supreme crisis from war and its threat, can the human family construct a more genuinely human world unless each person devotes himself with renewed determination to the true cause of peace?
gs-78-en: Is peace more than the absence of war or a balance of power between enemies, and is it rightly called an enterprise of justice resulting from the order structured into human society by its divine Founder?
gs-79-en: Now that every kind of weapon produced by modern science is used in war, does the fierce character of warfare threaten to lead combatants to a savagery far surpassing that of the past?
gs-80-en: Do acts of war involving scientific weapons that inflict massive and indiscriminate destruction go far beyond the bounds of legitimate defense, risking an almost total reciprocal slaughter of each side?
gs-81-en: Although the accumulation of arms may serve as a deterrent to possible enemy attack, must men be convinced that the arms race is not a safe way to preserve a steady peace, nor is the so-called balance resulting from this race a sure and authentic peace?
gs-82-en: Should support be given to the good will of the many leaders who work hard to do away with war, and are efforts already underway to eliminate the danger of war not to be underrated?
gs-83-en: To build up peace, must the causes of discord among men—especially injustice, excessive economic inequalities, the desire to dominate, and contempt for persons—be rooted out?
gs-84-en: Do the increasingly close ties of mutual dependence among all peoples now require that the community of nations organize itself in a manner suited to its present responsibilities, especially toward those still suffering from unbearable want?
gs-85-en: Does the present solidarity of mankind call for a revival of greater international cooperation in the economic field, since many peoples, though autonomous, are far from free of undue dependence?
gs-86-en: Should developing nations seek as the object of progress the total human fulfillment of their citizens, based not only on foreign aid but especially on full utilization of their own resources and their own culture?
gs-87-en: Is international cooperation urgently needed, especially for peoples undergoing pressures from rapid population increase, so that food and a suitable education can be furnished and shared with the entire human community?
gs-88-en: Should Christians cooperate willingly in establishing an international order that includes genuine respect for all freedoms and amicable brotherhood, since so much of the world still suffers from poverty as if Christ Himself were crying out in the poor?
gs-89-en: By preaching the Gospel and dispensing the treasures of grace, does the Church contribute to peace on earth and place fraternal exchange between men on solid ground by imparting knowledge of the divine and natural law?
gs-90-en: Is an outstanding form of international activity on the part of Christians found in joint efforts contributing to institutes that encourage cooperation among nations, including various Catholic associations on an international level?
gs-91-en: Do the proposals of this sacred synod, drawn from Church teaching, look to the assistance of every man of our time—whether he believes in God or does not explicitly recognize Him—to promote a sharper insight into full human destiny?
gs-92-en: By virtue of her mission to shed the radiance of the Gospel and to unify under one Spirit all men of whatever nation, race, or culture, does the Church stand forth as a sign of that brotherhood which allows honest dialogue and gives it vigor?
gs-93-en: By holding faithfully to the Gospel and joining with every man who loves and practices justice, have Christians shouldered a gigantic task demanding that they serve the men of the modern world with mounting generosity and success?
im-1-en: Among wonderful technological discoveries made with God's help, does the Church welcome and promote with special interest those media—such as the press, movies, radio, television, and the like—that most readily communicate news, views, and teachings?
im-2-en: Can the media of social communication, if properly utilized, be of great service to mankind for entertainment, instruction, and the spread of the Kingdom of God, even while they can also be employed contrary to the Creator's plan?
im-3-en: Does the Catholic Church consider it one of her duties to announce the Good News of salvation with the help of the media of social communication, and does she have an inherent right to employ these media as necessary or useful for the education of Christians?
im-4-en: For the proper use of these media, must all who employ them be acquainted with the norms of morality and conscientiously put them into practice, considering the nature of what is communicated and the whole situation of persons, place, and time?
im-5-en: Must all parties concerned adopt a proper moral outlook on the use of these media, especially regarding information—the search for and reporting of the news—which has become most useful and often necessary for the progress of contemporary society?
im-6-en: Regarding the relationship between the so-called rights of art and the norms of morality, must all hold to the absolute primacy of the objective moral order, which surpasses and fittingly coordinates all other spheres of human affairs, including the arts?
im-7-en: Can the narration, description, or portrayal of moral evil through the media of social communication serve a deeper knowledge of humanity and reveal truth and goodness, yet must such presentations always be subject to moral restraint?
im-8-en: Since public opinion exercises great power today in every sphere of life, must every member of society fulfill the demands of justice and charity in this area and strive, through these media as well, to form and spread sound public opinion?
im-9-en: Do readers, viewers, and listeners who freely use these media have special obligations to favor presentations outstanding for moral goodness, knowledge, and artistic merit, and to avoid those that may cause spiritual harm?
im-10-en: Should those who use the media of communications, especially the young, accustom themselves to moderation and self-control, deepen their understanding of what they see, hear, or read, and learn to pass sound judgments on them?
im-11-en: Does the principal moral responsibility for the proper use of the media of social communication fall on newsmen, writers, actors, designers, producers, distributors, critics, and all others who play any part in producing and transmitting mass presentations?
im-12-en: Is the public authority bound by special responsibilities toward the common good regarding these media, including the duty to protect true and just freedom of information, especially freedom of the press?
im-13-en: Should all the children of the Church join without delay in a common work to make effective use of the media of social communication in various apostolic endeavors, as circumstances and conditions demand?
im-14-en: Should a good press be fostered, and should a truly Catholic press be set up and encouraged to form, support, and advance public opinion in accord with natural law and Catholic teaching and precepts?
im-15-en: Should priests, religious, and laymen equipped with the proper skills for adapting these media to the apostolate be appointed promptly, and ought laymen be afforded technical, doctrinal, and moral training for this purpose?
im-16-en: Should programs suitable for instructing audiences of different cultural backgrounds and ages in the proper use of these media—especially those designed for young people—be encouraged and organized according to Christian moral principles?
im-17-en: Are the Church's children obliged to maintain and assist Catholic newspapers, periodicals, film projects, and radio and television programs whose principal objective is to spread and defend the truth and foster Christian influence in human society?
im-18-en: Should there be celebrated each year in every diocese, by determination of the Bishops, a day on which the faithful are instructed in their responsibilities regarding the media of social communication and invited to pray and contribute funds for this cause?
im-19-en: In fulfilling his supreme pastoral charge with respect to the media of social communication, does the Sovereign Pontiff have at hand a special office of the Holy See whose duties and competence the Council asks him to extend to all such media?
im-20-en: Is it the task of the Bishops to watch over, promote, and guide works and undertakings regarding the media of social communication in their own dioceses, not excluding those under the direction of exempt religious?
im-21-en: Does this sacred Synod decree that national offices for affairs of the press, films, radio, and television be established everywhere and given every aid, so that the consciences of the faithful may be properly instructed regarding these media?
im-22-en: Since the effectiveness of these media reaches beyond national boundaries, should national offices cooperate among themselves on an international plane and work together with their own international Catholic associations approved by the Holy See?
im-23-en: So that the general principles and norms of this sacred Synod on the media of social communications may be put into effect, should the office of the Holy See mentioned in Number 19 issue a pastoral instruction with the assistance of experts from various countries?
im-24-en: Does this sacred Synod confidently expect that its instructions and norms on the media will be gladly accepted and religiously kept by all the Church's children, and does it invite all men of good will to turn these media solely to the good of society?
lg-1-en: Is Christ the Light of nations, and is the Church in Christ like a sacrament or as a sign and instrument both of a very closely knit union with God and of the unity of the whole human race?
lg-2-en: Did the eternal Father, by a free and hidden plan of His own wisdom and goodness, create the whole world in order to raise men to a participation of the divine life, and, after the Fall, continually offer helps to salvation in view of Christ the Redeemer?
lg-3-en: Did the Son, sent by the Father, inaugurate the Kingdom of heaven on earth and bring about redemption by His obedience, so that the Church—that is, the kingdom of Christ now present in mystery—grows visibly through the power of God in the world?
lg-4-en: When the work which the Father gave the Son to do on earth was accomplished, was the Holy Spirit sent on Pentecost so that He might continually sanctify the Church and give all who believe access through Christ in one Spirit to the Father?
lg-5-en: Did the Lord Jesus set the Church on its course by preaching the Good News of the coming of the Kingdom of God, so that in the word, works, and presence of Christ this kingdom was clearly open to the view of men?
lg-6-en: Is the inner nature of the Church made known to us in different images—such as a sheepfold whose one and indispensable door is Christ, a flock, a cultivated field, a building, and a family—prepared already in the books of the Prophets?
lg-7-en: In the human nature united to Himself, did the Son of God, by overcoming death through His own death and resurrection, redeem man and remold him into a new creation, making His brothers mystically the components of His own Body by communicating His Spirit?
lg-8-en: Did Christ the one Mediator establish and continually sustain His holy Church as a community of faith, hope, and charity with visible delineation, such that the hierarchical society and the Mystical Body of Christ are not two realities but one complex reality?
lg-9-en: Has it pleased God to bring men together as one people which acknowledges Him in truth and serves Him in holiness, rather than to make men holy and save them merely as individuals without bond or link between one another?
lg-10-en: Did Christ the Lord, High Priest taken from among men, make the new people "a kingdom and priests to God the Father," so that the baptized are consecrated as a spiritual house and a holy priesthood to offer spiritual sacrifices?
lg-11-en: Is it through the sacraments and the exercise of the virtues that the sacred nature and organic structure of the priestly community is brought into operation, with the faithful incorporated in the Church through baptism destined for the worship of the Christian religion?
lg-12-en: Does the holy people of God share also in Christ's prophetic office, and can the entire body of the faithful, anointed by the Holy One, not err in matters of belief when from the bishops to the last of the faithful they show universal agreement in matters of faith and morals?
lg-13-en: Are all men called to belong to the new people of God, which, while remaining one and only one, is to be spread throughout the whole world and must exist in all ages?
lg-14-en: Is the Church, now sojourning on earth as an exile, necessary for salvation, since Christ, present in His Body which is the Church, is the one Mediator and the unique way of salvation, affirming also the necessity of the Church by the necessity of faith and baptism?
lg-15-en: Does the Church recognize that in many ways she is linked with those who, being baptized, are honored with the name of Christian, though they do not profess the faith in its entirety or do not preserve unity of communion with the successor of Peter?
lg-16-en: Are those who have not yet received the Gospel related in various ways to the people of God, including the people to whom the testament and promises were given, those who acknowledge the Creator, and those who seek God with a sincere heart?
lg-17-en: As the Son was sent by the Father, did He also send the Apostles to make disciples of all nations, and has the Church received this solemn mandate of Christ to proclaim the saving truth from the apostles and must carry it out to the ends of the earth?
lg-18-en: For the nurturing and constant growth of the People of God, did Christ the Lord institute in His Church a variety of ministries endowed with sacred power, which serve their brethren so that all may arrive at salvation?
lg-19-en: Did the Lord Jesus appoint twelve apostles as a college or stable group, over which He placed Peter chosen from among them, and send them so that as sharers in His power they might make all peoples His disciples?
lg-20-en: Will the divine mission entrusted by Christ to the apostles last until the end of the world, and did the apostles take care to appoint successors so that the mission assigned to them might continue after their death?
lg-21-en: In the bishops, for whom priests are assistants, is Our Lord Jesus Christ, the Supreme High Priest, present in the midst of those who believe, preaching the word of God and administering the sacraments of faith through their excellent service?
lg-22-en: Just as St. Peter and the other apostles constitute one apostolic college, are the Roman Pontiff, the successor of Peter, and the bishops, the successors of the apostles, joined together in a similar way?
lg-23-en: Is the Roman Pontiff, as the successor of Peter, the perpetual and visible principle and foundation of unity of both the bishops and of the faithful, while individual bishops are the visible principle and foundation of unity in their particular churches?
lg-24-en: Do bishops, as successors of the apostles, receive from the Lord the mission to teach all nations and to preach the Gospel to every creature, so that all men may attain to salvation by faith, baptism, and the fulfilment of the commandments?
lg-25-en: Among the principal duties of bishops, does the preaching of the Gospel occupy an eminent place, and are bishops authentic teachers endowed with the authority of Christ who preach to the people committed to them the faith they must believe and put into practice?
lg-26-en: Is a bishop marked with the fullness of the sacrament of Orders "the steward of the grace of the supreme priesthood," especially in the Eucharist, and is the Church of Christ truly present in all legitimate local congregations of the faithful united with their pastors?
lg-27-en: Do bishops, as vicars and ambassadors of Christ, govern the particular churches entrusted to them by their counsel, exhortations, example, and even by their authority and sacred power, which they personally exercise in Christ's name?
lg-28-en: Has Christ, through His apostles, made their successors the bishops partakers of His consecration and His mission, so that the divinely established ecclesiastical ministry is exercised on different levels by bishops, priests, and deacons?
lg-29-en: At a lower level of the hierarchy, are deacons those upon whom hands are imposed "not unto the priesthood, but unto a ministry of service," strengthened by sacramental grace to serve in the diaconate of the liturgy, of the word, and of charity?
lg-30-en: Besides what is said of the People of God in general, are there certain things which pertain in a special way to the laity, both men and women, by reason of their condition and mission?
lg-31-en: Is the term laity understood to mean all the faithful except those in holy orders and those in the state of religious life specially approved by the Church, who by baptism are made sharers in the priestly, prophetical, and kingly functions of Christ?
lg-32-en: By divine institution, is Holy Church ordered and governed with a wonderful diversity, so that the chosen People of God is one—"one Lord, one faith, one baptism"—sharing a common dignity as members from their regeneration in Christ?
lg-33-en: Are the laity gathered together in the People of God and made up as the Body of Christ under one head, called as living members to expend all their energy for the growth of the Church, with the lay apostolate a participation in the salvific mission of the Church itself?
lg-34-en: Does Christ Jesus, the supreme and eternal Priest, give the laity a sharing in His priestly function of offering spiritual worship for the glory of God and the salvation of men?
lg-35-en: Does Christ the great Prophet continually fulfill His prophetic office not only through the hierarchy who teach in His name, but also through the laity whom He made His witnesses and to whom He gave understanding of the faith (sensus fidei)?
lg-36-en: Has Christ communicated His royal power to His disciples so that they might be constituted in royal freedom and by true penance and a holy life conquer the reign of sin in themselves?
lg-37-en: Do the laity have the right, as do all Christians, to receive in abundance from their spiritual shepherds the spiritual goods of the Church, especially the assistance of the word of God and of the sacraments?
lg-38-en: Must each individual layman stand before the world as a witness to the resurrection and life of the Lord Jesus and a symbol of the living God, and must all the laity nourish the world with spiritual fruits?
lg-39-en: Is the Church believed to be indefectibly holy because Christ loved the Church as His bride, delivered Himself up for her that He might sanctify her, and united her to Himself as His own body?
lg-40-en: Did the Lord Jesus preach holiness of life to each and every one of His disciples of every condition, standing as the author and consummator of this holiness: "Be you therefore perfect, even as your heavenly Father is perfect"?
lg-41-en: Though the classes and duties of life are many, is holiness one—that sanctity cultivated by all who are moved by the Spirit of God—so that every person must walk according to his own personal gifts and duties in the path of living faith?
lg-42-en: Is the first and most necessary gift love, by which we love God above all things and our neighbor because of God, since God pours out His love into our hearts through the Holy Spirit who has been given to us?
lg-43-en: Are the evangelical counsels of chastity dedicated to God, poverty, and obedience based upon the words and examples of the Lord, and are they a divine gift which the Church received from its Lord and always safeguards with the help of His grace?
lg-44-en: When the faithful of Christ bind themselves to the evangelical counsels by vows or other sacred bonds like vows in purpose, is that person totally dedicated to God, loved beyond all things, under a new and special title?
lg-45-en: Is it the duty of the ecclesiastical hierarchy to regulate the practice of the evangelical counsels by law, since it is the duty of that hierarchy to care for the People of God and to lead them to most fruitful pastures?
lg-46-en: Does the Church present Christ to believers and non-believers alike in a striking manner daily through religious, portraying Christ in contemplation, in proclamation of the kingdom, in healing, in converting sinners, and in solicitude for all men?
lg-47-en: Should each of the faithful called to the profession of the evangelical counsels carefully see to it that he persevere and ever grow in that vocation God has given him, for the increased holiness of the Church and the greater glory of the Trinity?
lg-48-en: Will the Church attain its full perfection only in the glory of heaven, when there will come the time of the restoration of all things and the human race as well as the entire world will be perfectly reestablished in Christ?
lg-49-en: Until the Lord comes in His majesty, are some of His disciples exiles on earth, some having died being purified, and others in glory beholding God Himself triune and one, yet all in communion in the same charity of God and neighbor?
lg-50-en: Has the pilgrim Church from the very first ages cultivated with great piety the memory of the dead and offered suffrages for them, and has she always believed that the apostles and Christ's martyrs are closely joined with us in Christ?
lg-51-en: Does this Sacred Council accept with great devotion the venerable faith of our ancestors regarding fellowship with brethren in heavenly glory or still being purified, and propose again the decrees of Nicaea II, Florence, and Trent on this matter?
lg-52-en: Wishing to effect the redemption of the world, did God send His Son, born of a woman, that we might receive the adoption of sons, so that this divine mystery of salvation is revealed to us and continued in the Church which the Lord established as His body?
lg-53-en: Is the Virgin Mary, who at the message of the angel received the Word of God in her heart and in her body and gave Life to the world, acknowledged and honored as being truly the Mother of God and Mother of the Redeemer?
lg-54-en: In expounding the doctrine on the Church, does this Holy Synod intend to describe diligently both the role of the Blessed Virgin in the mystery of the Incarnate Word and the Mystical Body, and the duties of redeemed mankind toward the Mother of God?
lg-55-en: Do the Sacred Scriptures of both the Old and the New Testament, as well as ancient Tradition, show the role of the Mother of the Saviour in the economy of salvation in an ever clearer light?
lg-56-en: Did the Father of mercies will that the incarnation should be preceded by the acceptance of her who was predestined to be the mother of His Son, so that just as a woman contributed to death, so also a woman should contribute to life?
lg-57-en: Is the union of the Mother with the Son in the work of salvation made manifest from the time of Christ's virginal conception up to His death, as when Mary is greeted by Elizabeth as blessed because of her belief in the promise of salvation?
lg-58-en: In the public life of Jesus, does Mary make significant appearances, as at Cana when by her intercession she brought about the beginning of Jesus the Messiah's miracles?
lg-59-en: Before Pentecost, do we see the apostles persevering in prayer with the women and Mary the Mother of Jesus, with Mary by her prayers imploring the gift of the Spirit, and was the Immaculate Virgin preserved free from all guilt of original sin taken up body and soul into heavenly glory?
lg-60-en: Is there but one Mediator, the man Christ Jesus, and does the maternal duty of Mary toward men in no wise obscure or diminish this unique mediation of Christ, but rather show His power?
lg-61-en: Predestined from eternity to be the Mother of God, was the Blessed Virgin on this earth the virgin Mother of the Redeemer and, above all others and in a singular way, the generous associate and humble handmaid of the Lord?
lg-62-en: Did Mary's maternity in the order of grace begin with the consent she gave in faith at the Annunciation and sustain without wavering beneath the cross, and by her constant intercession after being taken up to heaven does she continue to bring us the gifts of eternal salvation?
lg-63-en: By reason of the gift and role of divine maternity, is the Blessed Virgin also intimately united with the Church, and as St. Ambrose taught, is the Mother of God a type of the Church in the order of faith, charity, and perfect union with Christ?
lg-64-en: By receiving the word of God in faith, does the Church herself become a mother, bringing forth to a new and immortal life the sons born to her in baptism, and is she herself a virgin who keeps the faith given to her by her Spouse whole and entire?
lg-65-en: While in the most holy Virgin the Church has already reached that perfection whereby she is without spot or wrinkle, do the followers of Christ still strive to increase in holiness by conquering sin, and so turn their eyes to Mary as the model of virtues?
lg-66-en: Placed by the grace of God as God's Mother next to her Son and exalted above all angels and men, is Mary justly honored by a special cult in the Church, from earliest times under the title of Mother of God?
lg-67-en: Does this most Holy Synod admonish all the sons of the Church that the cult, especially the liturgical cult, of the Blessed Virgin be generously fostered, and that practices of piety recommended by the magisterium toward her be made of great moment?
lg-68-en: Just as the Mother of Jesus, glorified in body and soul in heaven, is the image and beginning of the Church as it is to be perfected in the world to come, does she also shine forth on earth as a sign of sure hope and solace to the people of God during its sojourn?
lg-69-en: Does the entire body of the faithful pour forth instant supplications to the Mother of God and Mother of men that she, who aided the beginnings of the Church by her intercession, may now also implore unity among all who believe in Christ?
lg-appendix-notifications-en: Must the Council's text in the Schema de Ecclesia always be interpreted in accordance with the general rules that are known to all, as the Theological Commission responded regarding the precise theological note of the doctrine set forth?
lg-nota-intro-en: Did the Theological Commission decide to preface the assessment of the Modi with general observations clarifying the sense of collegiality in the Constitution on the Church?
lg-nota-1-en: Is "College" not understood in a strictly juridical sense as a group of equals who entrust their power to their president, but as a stable group whose structure and authority must be learned from Revelation?
lg-nota-2-en: Does a person become a member of the College by virtue of episcopal consecration and by hierarchical communion with the head of the College and with its members, receiving in consecration an ontological participation in the sacred functions (munera)?
lg-nota-3-en: Does the College, which does not exist without the head, exist also as the subject of supreme and full power in the universal Church, always and of necessity including its head, the Roman Pontiff, who preserves unhindered his function as Christ's Vicar?
lg-nota-4-en: As Supreme Pastor of the Church, can the Supreme Pontiff always exercise his power at will, as his very office demands, while the College acts as a college in the strict sense only from time to time and only with the consent of its head?
na-1-en: In our time, as mankind is drawn closer together, does the Church examine more closely her relationship to non-Christian religions, considering above all what men have in common and what draws them to fellowship?
na-2-en: From ancient times, is there found among various peoples a certain perception of that hidden power which hovers over the course of things and over the events of human history, and have religions bound up with advanced culture struggled to answer the restless searchings of the human heart?
na-3-en: Does the Church regard with esteem also the Moslems, who adore the one God, living and subsisting in Himself, merciful and all-powerful, the Creator of heaven and earth, who has spoken to men?
na-4-en: Does the Church of Christ acknowledge that, according to God's saving design, the beginnings of her faith and her election are found already among the Patriarchs, Moses, and the prophets, remembering the spiritual bond that ties the people of the New Covenant to Abraham's stock?
na-5-en: Can we truly call on God, the Father of all, if we refuse to treat in a brotherly way any man created in the image of God, and does any theory or practice that leads to discrimination between man and man as to human dignity and the rights flowing from it lack foundation?
oe-1-en: Does the Catholic Church hold in high esteem the institutions, liturgical rites, ecclesiastical traditions, and established standards of Christian life of the Eastern Churches, in which remains conspicuous the tradition handed down from the Apostles through the Fathers?
oe-2-en: Is the Holy Catholic Church, the Mystical Body of Christ, made up of the faithful organically united in the Holy Spirit by the same faith, sacraments, and government, who form separate Churches or Rites held together by a hierarchy, with variety in no way harming unity?
oe-3-en: Are the individual Churches of East and West, though differing somewhat in rite, liturgy, discipline, and spiritual heritage, each as much as the others entrusted to the pastoral government of the Roman Pontiff and consequently of equal dignity?
oe-4-en: Should means be taken in every part of the world for the protection and advancement of all the individual Churches, establishing parishes and a special hierarchy where the spiritual good of the faithful demands it?
oe-5-en: Does this Sacred Council solemnly declare that the Churches of the East, as much as those of the West, fully enjoy the right and are in duty bound to rule themselves, each in accordance with its own established disciplines?
oe-6-en: Can and should all members of the Eastern Rite always preserve their legitimate liturgical rite and their established way of life, which may not be altered except to obtain for themselves an organic improvement?
oe-7-en: Has the patriarchate as an institution existed in the Church from the earliest times and been recognized by the first ecumenical councils, the Eastern patriarch being the bishop with jurisdiction over all bishops, clergy, and people of his own territory or rite, without prejudice to the primacy of the Roman Pontiff?
oe-8-en: Though some patriarchates of the Eastern Churches are of earlier and some of later date, are all nonetheless equal in respect of patriarchal dignity, without prejudice to the legitimately established precedence of honor?
oe-9-en: By the most ancient tradition of the Church, are the patriarchs of the Eastern Churches to be accorded special honor as father and head of their patriarchate, and should their rights and privileges be re-established in accordance with ancient tradition and the decrees of the ecumenical councils?
oe-10-en: Is what has been said of patriarchs also valid, in harmony with the canon law, in respect to major archbishops who rule the whole of some individual church or rite?
oe-11-en: Seeing that the patriarchal office in the Eastern Church is a traditional form of government, does this Sacred Ecumenical Council ardently desire that new patriarchates should be erected where there is need, by an ecumenical council or by the Roman Pontiff?
oe-12-en: Does this Sacred Ecumenical Council confirm and approve the ancient discipline of the sacraments existing in the Oriental Churches, as also the ritual practices connected with their celebration and administration?
oe-13-en: Should the established practice regarding the minister of Confirmation that has obtained from most early times in the Eastern Church be fully restored, so that priests validly confer this sacrament using chrism blessed by a patriarch or a bishop?
oe-14-en: Can all Eastern Rite priests, either in conjunction with Baptism or separately from it, validly confer Confirmation on all the faithful of any rite including the Latin, licitly only if the regulations of common and particular law are observed?
oe-15-en: Are the faithful bound to take part on Sundays and feast days in the Divine Liturgy or, according to the regulations or custom of their own rite, in the celebration of the Divine Office, with the precept extending from the Vespers of the vigil to the end of the Sunday or feast day?
oe-16-en: Do faculties for hearing confessions duly and without restriction given to priests of any rite by their own hierarchs extend to the whole territory of him who grants them and also to the places and faithful of any other rite in the same territory, unless the hierarch of the place has expressly excluded this?
oe-17-en: Does this Sacred Council ardently desire that the office of the permanent diaconate should, where it has fallen into disuse in the Eastern Churches, be restored, so that the ancient established practice of the Sacrament of Orders may flourish again?
oe-18-en: When Eastern Catholics marry baptized Eastern non-Catholics, is the canonical "form" for the celebration of these marriages of obligation only for liceity, with the presence of a sacred minister sufficient for validity, provided other prescriptions of law are observed?
oe-19-en: Does it belong only to an ecumenical council or to the Apostolic See to determine, transfer, or suppress feast days common to all the Eastern Churches, while feast days of individual churches also fall within the competence of the patriarchal or archiepiscopal synod?
oe-20-en: Until all Christians are agreed on a fixed day for Easter, may the patriarchs or supreme authorities of a place, by unanimous consent of those affected, agree to celebrate the feast of Easter on the same Sunday to promote unity among Christians of the same area or nation?
oe-21-en: May individual faithful dwelling outside the area or territory of their own rite follow completely the established custom of the place where they live as regards the law of the sacred seasons, and in families of mixed rite observe this law according to one and the same rite?
oe-22-en: Should Eastern clerics and Religious celebrate the Divine Office in accordance with the prescriptions and traditions of their own established custom, and should the faithful too assist devoutly as occasion allows at the Divine Office?
oe-23-en: Does it belong to the patriarch with his synod, or to the supreme authority of each church with the council of the hierarchs, to regulate the use of languages in the sacred liturgical functions and, after reference to the Apostolic See, to approve translations of texts into the vernacular?
oe-24-en: Do the Eastern Churches in communion with the Apostolic See of Rome have a special duty of promoting the unity of all Christians, especially Eastern Christians, by prayer, example of life, religious fidelity to ancient Eastern traditions, greater knowledge of each other, and collaboration?
oe-25-en: If any separated Eastern Christian joins himself to the unity of Catholics under the guidance of the Holy Spirit, should no more be required of him than what a bare profession of the Catholic faith demands, and may Eastern clerics exercise the Orders they possess on joining, since a valid priesthood is preserved among them?
oe-26-en: Is common participation in worship (communicatio in sacris) which harms the unity of the Church or involves formal acceptance of error or the danger of aberration in the faith, of scandal, and of indifferentism forbidden by divine law, while pastoral experience shows individual cases among Eastern brethren must also be considered?
oe-27-en: May Eastern Christians separated in good faith from the Catholic Church, if they ask of their own accord and have the right dispositions, be admitted to Penance, the Eucharist, and the Anointing of the Sick, and may Catholics ask these same sacraments from non-Catholic ministers whose churches possess valid sacraments when necessity requires it?
oe-28-en: Given the same principles, is common participation by Catholics with their Eastern separated brethren in sacred functions, things, and places allowed for a just cause?
oe-29-en: Is this conciliatory policy with regard to communicatio in sacris with the brethren of the separated Eastern Churches put into the care and control of the local hierarchs, so that by combined counsel they may direct relations among Christians by timely and effective regulations?
oe-30-en: Are all these directives of law laid down in view of the present situation until the Catholic Church and the separated Eastern Churches come together into complete unity, and are all Christians earnestly asked meanwhile to pray to God fervently for that full unity?
ot-1-en: Is a special "program of priestly training" to be undertaken by each country or rite, set up by the episcopal conferences, revised from time to time, and approved by the Apostolic See, so that universal laws may be adapted to particular circumstances?
ot-2-en: Does the duty of fostering vocations pertain to the whole Christian community, exercised above all by a fully Christian life, with the principal contributors being families that become a kind of initial seminary, and the parishes in whose rich life young people take part?
ot-3-en: In minor seminaries erected to develop the seeds of vocations, should students be prepared by special religious formation, particularly through appropriate spiritual direction, to follow Christ the Redeemer with generosity of spirit and purity of heart?
ot-4-en: Are major seminaries necessary for priestly formation, and should the entire training of the students there be oriented to the formation of true shepherds of souls after the model of our Lord Jesus Christ, teacher, priest, and shepherd?
ot-5-en: Since the training of students depends most of all on qualified educators, are the administrators and teachers of seminaries to be selected from the best men and carefully prepared in sound doctrine, suitable pastoral experience, and special spiritual and pedagogical training?
ot-6-en: With watchful concern for each candidate's age and stage of progress, should inquiry be made into his proper intention and freedom of choice, his spiritual, moral, and intellectual qualifications, his physical and psychic health, and his ability to bear the priestly burdens?
ot-7-en: Where individual dioceses are unable to institute their own seminaries properly, are seminaries for many dioceses or for an entire region or country to be set up and developed so that the sound training of the students can be taken care of more effectively?
ot-8-en: Should the spiritual training of seminarians be closely connected with the doctrinal and pastoral, imparted so that students might learn to live in an intimate and unceasing union with the Father through His Son Jesus Christ in the Holy Spirit?
ot-9-en: Should seminarians be so saturated with the mystery of the Church that, bound to the Vicar of Christ in humble and trusting charity and later adhering to their own bishop as faithful helpers, they bear witness to that unity that attracts men to Christ?
ot-10-en: Are students who follow the venerable tradition of celibacy according to the holy and fixed laws of their own rite to be educated to this state with great care, renouncing the companionship of marriage for the sake of the kingdom of heaven?
ot-11-en: Are the norms of Christian education to be religiously observed and properly complemented by the newer findings of sound psychology and pedagogy, so that by wisely planned training a due human maturity may also be developed in the students?
ot-12-en: Will it be the prerogative of the bishops to establish a fitting period of time for a more intense introduction to the spiritual life, and to determine the opportuneness of providing for a certain interruption in the studies or a suitable introduction to pastoral work?
ot-13-en: Before beginning specifically ecclesiastical subjects, should seminarians be equipped with that humanistic and scientific training which young men in their own countries are wont to have as a foundation for higher studies, and acquire a knowledge of Latin enabling them to understand the sources of so many sciences and the documents of the Church?
ot-14-en: In revising ecclesiastical studies, should the philosophical and theological disciplines be more suitably aligned so that they harmoniously open more and more the minds of the students to the mystery of Christ?
ot-15-en: Are the philosophical disciplines to be taught so that students first acquire a solid and coherent knowledge of man, the world, and of God, relying on a philosophical patrimony which is perennially valid and taking into account the philosophical investigations of later ages?
ot-16-en: Should the theological disciplines, in the light of faith and under the guidance of the magisterium, be so taught that students correctly draw out Catholic doctrine from divine revelation, profoundly penetrate it, and be enabled to proclaim, explain, and protect it in their priestly ministry?
ot-17-en: Since doctrinal training ought to tend not to a mere communication of ideas but to a true and intimate formation of the students, are teaching methods to be revised as regards lectures, discussions, seminars, and the development of study privately or in small groups?
ot-18-en: Will it be the bishops' concern that young men suited by temperament, virtue, and ability be sent to special institutes, faculties, or universities so that priests may be trained at a higher scientific level in the sacred sciences and in other fields judged opportune?
ot-19-en: Does pastoral concern demand that seminarians be diligently instructed in matters particularly linked to the sacred ministry, especially in catechesis and preaching, liturgical worship and the administration of the sacraments, works of charity, and assisting the erring and the unbelieving?
ot-20-en: Should seminarians also be taught to use the aids which pedagogy, psychology, and sociology can provide, according to correct methodology and the norms of ecclesiastical authority, and be properly instructed in inspiring and fostering the apostolic activity of the laity?
ot-21-en: Since priestly training must be pursued and perfected even after the completion of seminary studies, will it be the responsibility of episcopal conferences in individual nations to employ suitable means to this end, such as pastoral institutes, meetings held at stated times, and appropriate projects?
ot-conclusion-en: Have the Fathers of this holy synod pursued the work of priestly formation begun by the Council of Trent, confidently entrusting to seminary administrators and teachers the task of forming the future priests of Christ in the spirit of the renewal promoted by this sacred synod?
pc-1-en: Does the pursuit of perfect charity through the evangelical counsels draw its origin from the doctrine and example of the Divine Master and reveal itself as a splendid sign of the heavenly kingdom?
pc-2-en: Does the adaptation and renewal of the religious life include both the constant return to the sources of all Christian life and to the original spirit of the institutes, and their adaptation to the changed conditions of our time?
pc-3-en: Should the manner of living, praying, and working be suitably adapted everywhere, but especially in mission territories, to the modern physical and psychological circumstances of the members and to the necessities of the apostolate, culture, and social and economic circumstances?
pc-4-en: Does an effective renewal and adaptation of religious life demand the cooperation of all the members of the institute, while establishing the norms of adaptation and embodying them in legislation belongs only to the competent authorities, especially to general chapters?
pc-5-en: By professing the evangelical counsels, have members of each institute responded to a divine call so that by being not only dead to sin but also renouncing the world they may live for God alone, in a special consecration deeply rooted in that of baptism?
pc-6-en: Should those who make profession of the evangelical counsels seek and love above all else God who has first loved us, and strive to foster in all circumstances a life hidden with Christ in God?
pc-7-en: Do communities entirely dedicated to contemplation, whose members in solitude and silence with constant prayer and penance occupy themselves with God alone, retain at all times an honorable place in the Mystical Body of Christ, no matter how pressing the needs of the active apostolate may be?
pc-8-en: Are there in the Church very many communities, both clerical and lay, which devote themselves to various apostolic tasks, possessing differing gifts according to the grace allotted to them?
